subject: AI & Agents
title: Your Data Is the Product
description: A micro-lesson that makes Your Data Is the Product usable.

hook.text: Every search, click, and scroll trains an AI model. Your behavior is the raw material.

buildup.text: Companies collect vast datasets of user behavior to train recommendation and ad-targeting models.

discovery.text: Terms of service agreements grant broad data usage rights that few people read.

twist.text: Your data doesn't just improve your experience — it trains models that affect millions of others.

climax.text: GDPR and other regulations try to give users control, but enforcement is inconsistent.

punchline.text: Free apps aren't free. You pay with your data.

quiz.question: How do companies use your behavioral data?
options: To train AI models for recommendations and ad targeting
Only to improve your personal experience
They delete it immediately after collection

details.summary: Free digital services profit by collecting user data and feeding it to AI systems. Your browsing, clicks, and conversations become the raw material that trains algorithms to predict and influence your behavior.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding data as currency empowers individuals to make informed choices about which services they use and what personal information they willingly share.
takeaways: Free services monetize user data through ads and AI training
Personal data feeds algorithms that predict your behavior
Understanding data economics empowers informed consent choices

faq.question: How do free apps and services make money from user data?
faq.answer: They sell targeted advertising powered by user profiles. Your behavior data trains AI models that predict what you will buy, watch, or click, making ad targeting extremely precise.

faq.question: Can you opt out of having your data used by AI?
faq.answer: Partially. GDPR and similar laws give some control over data usage. However, opting out of all data collection is nearly impossible while using modern digital services.
